messages.subject: model averaging Error
parts:
Hi all
I would like to  do model averaging of two best models
mod1=  (D~1 g0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2)
mod2 = (D~1 a0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2)
As we can see the detection parameters are not same hence in these two models, hence I only selected (D,sigma and pmix) as real and beta parameter.
But I find this error.
 m<-model.average(mod1, mod2, realnames = c("D","sigma","pmix"),betanames = c("D","sigma",pmix))
Error in model.average(mod1, mod2, realnames = c("D", "sigma", "pmix"),  :
  'model.average' cannot handle scaled detection parameters
Could you guide me how to do model averaging for these two models as there AIC differences are less than two.
,

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: model averaging Error
parts:
Hello Mayank

You've probably figured this out for yourself by now, but...

Firstly, the two models are the same and it makes no sense to average them. Using the 'captdata' dataset:
AIC(mod1, mod2)
                          model   detectfn npar    logLik      AIC     AICc dAICc AICcwt
mod1 D~1 g0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2 halfnormal    6 -758.4792 1528.958 1530.176     0    0.5
mod2 D~1 a0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2 halfnormal    6 -758.4792 1528.958 1530.176     0    0.5

This is because you make a0 unique to each mixture class (a0~h2) rather than constant (a0~1).

Secondly, model.average() does not handle the a0 parameterisation or 'scaled detection parameters' as they used to be called. If you want to average such models you have to do it by hand.

Thirdly, do not specify both realnames and betanames as arguments of model.average(). The help says "To average beta parameters, specify betanames (this is ignored if a value is provided for realnames)."

Murray
